Sheet: @UUID[Actor.Y53IKZpt8sl2sl65]{August Krell}

“He taught you to block the blow. He taught me to take it.”

Clan: Brujah · Sect: none · Role in @UUID[JournalEntry.ll97TEj4MRjtM595]{Chapter 7 · The Ward File}: antagonist; the false Vance

pages.name: Mortal Days: The Legionnaire of the Docks

text.content: August Krell was born in Hamburg in 1944, between bombing raids, and grew up in the port of Marseille, where his mother took him fleeing from everything. At seventeen he enlisted in the Foreign Legion under a false name and reached Algeria for the last year of the war. He came back with a medal he never wore and a strange calm about violence: he didn't enjoy hurting people, but it didn't cost him anything either. After that he worked as a longshoreman, as muscle for smugglers, and as whatever the docks needed.

In 1972, Marcus Vance (@UUID[JournalEntry.WIihWwv4LCOX68B1]{Marcus “Ironjaw” Vance}) watched him fight three men armed with iron bars in a dockside warehouse, and win. He Embraced him that same night. Krell is Vance's childe, like David. Nobody in Seattle knows, not even David.

Vance trained him for four years with the same doctrine, the same discipline, and the cold water. But in 1976 he decided Krell wasn't fit: the Beast asked him for permission too often, and he gave it too gladly. Vance taught him the inverted guard, the one given to those who don't finish (@UUID[JournalEntry.kzeWNRBY6tgLP37S]{Journal of M. Vance, Marseille, 1963, Folio 14 (Typewritten Copy)}), and left without saying goodbye.

Krell spent fifty years as a mercenary. He worked for Archons, for the Sabbat, for whoever paid. He killed a lot, and he killed well. He never stopped wondering what he'd done wrong. In early 2026, Mr. Pell, Halloway's archivist, found him in Lisbon: Vance's journals mention “the German” three times. Halloway offered him Vance's coat, which came in the same auction lot, a domain in Seattle, and, above all, the journal folios where Vance writes about him. Krell said yes before he finished the sentence.

Clean up the copies. He destroys the Kindred who buy or transport copies of the File, using Controlled Fury so it looks like Vance's work (@UUID[JournalEntry.5hwXPdn0tUJ3NaKZ.JournalEntryPage.DtetdHiBnOLQaM6Y]{A1-E02 · Ash on Pier 46}, @UUID[JournalEntry.FttkHsYSSaCpIugu.JournalEntryPage.j4TnqYOwVuSCeQ0z]{A2-E02 · “Locate. Evaluate. Execute.”}). Jun Takeda is his next target (Night 4).

Make his brother see him. He doesn't want to beat David; he wants David to acknowledge him. In @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.7brn5AgmWggUl420]{A3-E01 · The Other Son} he goes after one of the coterie's Touchstones to force David to look him in the face. In @UUID[JournalEntry.C7cxKf7kcAELzuJ1.JournalEntryPage.hAX2tLfjRPJ2o4Tr]{A3-E03 · Face to Face with Krell} he offers to talk. He demands David; the coterie decides whether to bring him and how. Krell only looks at David: the PCs talk and David confirms.

The folios. Halloway promised him the journal pages that talk about him and still hasn't handed them over. Krell is starting to suspect they don't exist, or that they say something Halloway doesn't want him to read. If the coterie shows him those folios, he switches sides (@UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.jXff6tMXQQbmJg0m]{Krell's Testimony}). If he also learns the other guard, he can become Allies 2 for the coterie.

The promised domain. Halloway promised him Harbor Island, David's domain. Krell hasn't yet asked himself how Halloway plans to keep that promise.

A rusted barge in dry dock in Georgetown, south of the port, which Halloway rents him through a shell company (Haven 1). He sleeps in the hold, in a toolbox the size of a coffin. He feeds on night-shift longshoremen and truckers. He finds them alone, hits them once, hard, and drinks fast. He doesn't kill anyone unless he has to. He finds it unprofessional.

Vance's coat: a long gray wool coat, tailored for a man broader in the shoulders. It's too big for him. It's “the coat that isn't his” from @UUID[JournalEntry.BxMkvzNl7Yt8OyTI]{r/SeattleAfterDark: “Anyone Else See This on Harbor Island?”} and @UUID[JournalEntry.FVBnf3yE87K4BOhh]{Wendell Fry: “Song for the Son of the Fist”}.

Copy 2 of 3 of Vance's journals (@UUID[JournalEntry.kzeWNRBY6tgLP37S]{Journal of M. Vance, Marseille, 1963, Folio 14 (Typewritten Copy)}), with his pencil notes.

Halloway's support: an electric car with no registered plates, and two security ghouls (@UUID[Actor.BzNGxOAK3F6Uo56T]{Halloway's Security Ghouls}) if he asks for them.

Resources 1: what Halloway pays him.

Marcus Vance (wounded love). He hates him and needs him. He believes Vance is dead and isn't sure that changes anything.

David Smith (envy). The one who finished. The one who got the other guard. The good son.

Charles Halloway (distrust). He knows he's being used. He doesn't care, as long as Halloway gives him the folios.

Hal Brekke (respect). He watches Hal track from a distance, and Hal reminds him of the good legionnaires.

Rosa Iturbe (indifference). He knows Halloway is using her as a scapegoat. It's none of his business.

• “Vance came back and he's cleaning up the city.” (False. It's Krell.)
  • “The dock killer fights with his left side forward.” (True: it's the inverted guard, @UUID[JournalEntry.j32Ohis1qKJB3jcx.JournalEntryPage.HYE4rNbNf1sEbYGe]{The Inverted Guard}.)
  • “The killer works for the Everett Anarchs.” (False. Halloway is running him.)
  • “There's an old Brujah sleeping on a barge in Georgetown.” (True. The Nosferatu know, and they sell it dear.)

He has no Mask (Mask 0); he uses forged papers from a Portuguese passport. He looks about twenty-eight, but he moves like someone older. His head is shaved, an old knife scar cuts across his left eyebrow, his broken nose healed badly, and his hands are full of broken knuckles. He wears dark work clothes under Vance's coat. He's left-handed. He says little, with a French accent, and when he's serious he drops his voice so low you have to lean in. He smells of wet wool.

Editor's Note

Doc 07 said “looks about thirty-five”; it was decided that he looks the age he was at his Embrace (1972, born in 1944): about twenty-eight.

• Sire: Marcus “Ironjaw” Vance (@UUID[JournalEntry.WIihWwv4LCOX68B1]{Marcus “Ironjaw” Vance})
  • Embraced: 1972 (born in 1944)
  • Ambition: for someone to acknowledge that he was Vance's son too.
  • Convictions: “A job gets finished” · “Never hit someone who can't hit back.”
  • Touchstone: none living. The last was his mother, who died in 1981. Krell has lost a great deal of Humanity since then.
  • Humanity: 4
  • Generation: 9th
  • Blood Potency: 3

Attributes: Strength 5, Dexterity 4, Stamina 4 · Charisma 2, Manipulation 2, Composure 3 · Intelligence 2, Wits 4, Resolve 3

Secondary Attributes: Health 7 · Willpower 6

Skills: Firearms 3, Athletics 4, Streetwise 2 (Docks), Awareness 3, Intimidation 4 (Silence), Brawl 5 (Incomplete Controlled Fury), Melee 3 (Bars and knives), Stealth 4, Survival 2

Disciplines:

  • Potence 4: Lethal Body (Lethal Body), Soaring Leap (Soaring Leap), Prowess (Prowess), Draught of Might (Draught of Might)
  • Celerity 3: Cat's Grace (Cat's Grace), Fleetness (Fleetness), Blink (Blink)
  • Presence 2: Daunt (Daunt), Lingering Kiss (Lingering Kiss)

The inverted guard (special rule): against an opponent who knows the complete doctrine of Controlled Fury (any PC with @UUID[JournalEntry.x7rVnQfKbb3HdbG5.JournalEntryPage.oGnroV6R68YdMQyD]{LOR-01 · The Doctrine of Controlled Fury} at level 4 or higher), Krell loses 2 dice from all his close-combat defense pools. David knows it too, but he doesn't roll: the Storyteller narrates what he does, and Krell loses those 2 dice against the PC who attacks alongside David. Krell knows this, and that's why he avoids fighting David head-on if he can.

Editor's Note · LOR-01 Level and Disciplines

The chapter 4 sheet (doc 07) called for LOR-01 at level 3 or higher. Chapter 7 (doc 10) and the combat version in chapter 8 (doc 14) call for level 4 or higher, which is the level of “The Complete Guard” on the Loresheet (doc 08). The newest doc wins: level 4.

Doc 07 gave him five powers at Potence 4 and four at Celerity 3; in V5 there's one per dot. Spark of Rage (Spark of Rage) was removed, since it's an amalgam that requires Presence 3 and Krell has Presence 2, and so was Rapid Reflexes (Rapid Reflexes). In Celerity, Blink is the only one named by the scenes and the combat version; of the other three, Cat's Grace and Fleetness fit his rooftop escapes, and Rapid Reflexes is the one he uses least.

Quick pools: Unarmed attack 10 (Strength + Brawl, plus Prowess) · Initiative and defense 7 · Stealth 8
